solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A&E discharged water engineer after mishap in plant

indicators.note: a mishap leaves things in disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
discharged means sent out, so these letters leave the phrase water engineer

parts.note: A&E stands for the letters A and E

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency department sends home a water engineer injured in an accident at an industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' removes A and E from WATER ENGINEER; 'after mishap' shuffles the remaining eleven letters. 'plant' suggests a factory but is a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is a low evergreen shrub whose leaves yield an aromatic oil, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Dream one shares

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal is to share out, so with 'one' as subject, 'one shares' reads as I deal

explanation.surface: A dream of something one has in common with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one shares' reads as a pronoun and verb, 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect vision one aspires to, a dream in the sense of a cherished aim.

clue.text: Hot time on island with footloose Ali …

parts.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy

indicators.note: footloose means losing the foot, the bottom letter of the down word Ali

explanation.surface: A boxer called Ali, free and easy, enjoys a hot holiday on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'foot' of ALI is its last letter. The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal describes heat, as in thermal springs, so it means hot.

clue.text: … get hot again with Heather — topless and uninhibited!

indicators.note: uninhibited means free, so the remaining letters are let loose and rearranged
topless means losing the top letter of the word Heather

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, things heat up again with a woman called Heather going topless and wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first H, leaving EATHER; 'uninhibited' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat is to warm up again, so to get hot again.

clue.text: Cycle race's start ain't too haphazard

indicators.note: the start of race's is its first letter
haphazard means random, so the letters of ain't too are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cycle race begins in a slapdash way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle race' reads as a bike event; 'Cycle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is one complete turn or a recurring sequence, both senses of a cycle.

clue.text: Bighead, say, is too much around

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: around says the letters for too much wrap round is

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A conceited person's ego is said to be excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top', excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bighead is a conceited person who talks constantly about themselves, a self-centred egotist.

clue.text: Spotting problem at the Pole?

parts.note: spotting means seeing; glare from polar ice and snow can stop an explorer seeing

explanation.surface: A puzzle about spots, perhaps a skin complaint, near the North Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotting' suggests pimples or stains; it means sighting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare from sunlit snow damages the eyes, a sight problem common in polar regions.

clue.text: Feign illness — no good turning up for detractor

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the letters for no good upwards, swapping their order

parts.note: to malinger is to pretend to be ill to avoid work

explanation.surface: Someone shirks work by pretending to be sick, and is no use when they do show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' sounds like arriving, but in this down clue it means the no-good letters are flipped in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A maligner speaks ill of others, a critic who belittles, which is a detractor.

clue.text: Infection from 'the crancium'?

parts.note: the made-up word crancium is cranium with a C, the abbreviation for cold, placed inside it

explanation.surface: A pretend medical term for an ailment of the skull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crancium' is cranium (head) with C for cold inside it, so a cold sits in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday name for the common cold when it causes congestion and a blocked nose.

clue.text: Relative or precise about English?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is placed around the letter for English

parts.note: nice can mean precise or subtle, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: A question whether a family member is particular about the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precise' uses the older sense of nice, fine or exact, as in 'a nice point'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, an example of a relative.

clue.text: Dish a turn over controversy

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew baked under sliced potatoes, a Lancashire dish
TO is short for turn over, as in PTO, please turn over

explanation.surface: A meal goes around the table during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: HOTPOT is a lamb and potato stew from Lancashire in northern England. PTO, 'please turn over', printed at the foot of a page, gives TO for 'turn over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a contentious issue nobody wants to handle, so it fits a controversy.

clue.text: Source malicious, though at first kindly intended

parts.note: a well is a source of water
mean can mean spiteful or malicious

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word though

explanation.surface: Someone's informant had bad motives, though the remark seemed kind initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' and 'malicious' look like one phrase about a spiteful informant; they are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant with good intentions, even if it misfires, is described with this idiom for kindly intended.

clue.text: Cressida I liked rather in comeback for epic

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the hidden letters are read backwards
in tells us the letters sit inside the words Cressida I liked

explanation.surface: A reader says they preferred Cressida when she reappeared, as if in a sequel to an epic.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Cressida I liked' from right to left: the letters ending Cressida, the I and the start of liked spell the answer. Cressida belongs to the Trojan story, which is the answer's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is the classic example of an epic poem.

clue.text: To sum up, cut twisted nonsense from tall story and rewrite

indicators.note: rewrite tells us to rearrange what remains into new letters
cut says to remove letters from the phrase tall story
twisted says the synonym for nonsense is turned round

parts.note: rot is a British word for nonsense

explanation.surface: An editor is told to trim the rubbish from an exaggerated tale and redraft it, in summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns ROT into TOR; 'cut' takes T, O and R out of TALL STORY, leaving TALLSY, which 'rewrite' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly introduces a final point, as does the phrase to sum up at the end of an argument.

clue.text: Showy stand-in sets up net alternately with staff

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of the words sets up net

parts.note: to man something is to staff it, as in manning a desk

explanation.surface: A theatrical understudy erects a net, taking turns with the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a noun for personnel but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman stands in for an actor in dangerous, spectacular scenes, a showy kind of substitute.

clue.text: Crib score (high one) a possibility; get it!

parts.note: a crib is a child's bed, a cot
a ton is a score of a hundred, a high one in darts or cricket
something that is on is possible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A cribbage player hopes for a big score and urges a partner to grasp the chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crib' and 'score' suggest the card game cribbage. 'Ton' is British slang for a hundred, a top score in darts or cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is informal British for to understand, the same as the exclamation get it.

clue.text: Writer opening up about desire

indicators.note: about says the reversed opening goes round the word for desire
in a down clue up means the word for opening is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a vent is an opening, as in an air vent
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: An author starts to open up about his longings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening up' reads as confiding; in a down clue 'up' means the opening word reads bottom to top before it wraps round the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons, so a writer.

clue.text: Mollusc appears as gold among shimmering sunlit surroundings

indicators.note: among says the symbol for gold goes in the middle
surroundings says the rearranged letters enclose the gold
shimmering suggests movement, so the letters of sunlit are rearranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A shellfish gleams golden in rippling sunlit water around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears as' is link glue; 'surroundings' confirms the shuffled letters go round the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The chambered nautilus is a cephalopod with a spiral shell, a marine mollusc.

clue.text: Searching in damaged Pathfinder, RAF ordered to abort

indicators.note: damaged suggests breaking, so the letters of Pathfinder are rearranged
ordered to abort says the letters of RAF are taken out of Pathfinder

explanation.surface: An RAF Pathfinder bomber, damaged, is told to call off its mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Pathfinders were RAF squadrons marking targets in WWII. 'ordered to abort' removes R, A, F, leaving PTHINDE, which 'damaged' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A searching inquiry is thorough and detailed, which is what an in-depth one is.

clue.text: Char takes whisky with Rector where time's immaterial

indicators.note: immaterial says time does not matter, so its letter is dropped for another

parts.note: Scotch is whisky from Scotland
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady, a char, drinks whisky with the parish rector, heedless of the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the British cleaning woman of the surface but is the verb to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To char something is to burn its surface, which is a synonym of scorching it.

clue.text: Band gathers round Gorbachev and Ronald's meeting-place

indicators.note: gathers round keeps the tail of Gorbachev, the letters gathered round the point where the names meet
the meeting place of the two names keeps only the start of Ronald, where it joins the end of the Russian's name

explanation.surface: A band encircles the summit venue of Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of Gorbachev meets the start of Ronald where the two names join; 'and' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe, a band on a uniform sleeve or a heraldic shield.

clue.text: Glass Menagerie's opening in Richmond for starters, then two runs across Ohio

indicators.note: the opening of Menagerie's is its first letter
for starters takes the first letter of each of in and Richmond
across says the two letters for runs span the letter for Ohio
two says the abbreviation for runs appears twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the initial of Ohio, the US state

explanation.surface: A production of The Glass Menagerie opens in Richmond, then two runs in Ohio follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass Menagerie' is Tennessee Williams's play; only 'Glass' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass is an older word for a mirror.

clue.text: Marked dip borders sides of terrace

indicators.note: borders means goes around the edges, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to nod is to dip the head

indicators.note: sides of means the outer letters of the word terrace

explanation.surface: A noticeable dip runs alongside the edges of a garden terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marked' as an adjective suggests noticeable; here it means observed.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is marked, it is observed or remarked upon, the same as being noted.

clue.text: Landing direction of 'Godspell', Lloyd is delightedly choosing leads, the PA elaborated

indicators.note: choosing leads means taking the leading letter of each of the four words
elaborated means worked up into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Andrew Lloyd Webber gleefully directs a production of the musical Godspell, with a personal assistant making the arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborated' rearranges THE PA to give EPATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft follow a set descending route onto the runway, a flight path that directs the landing.

clue.text: Spirit of the moon?

definitions.meaning: the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest
one of the satellites of the planet Uranus

explanation.surface: A question about the soul of the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Uranus's moons are named after Shakespeare characters, so the spirit and the moon share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is Prospero's spirit in The Tempest and also a moon of Uranus named after him.

clue.text: Steel pans beginning to rattle here, confusedly

indicators.note: confusedly says the gathered letters before it are mixed up

parts.note: the word pans, the first letter of rattle (its beginning) and the word here make one pool of letters

explanation.surface: Steel pans in a band start to clatter here in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel pans' reads as the Caribbean instruments, but 'Steel' alone is the definition. 'beginning to rattle' supplies R, which joins PANS and HERE before 'confusedly' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel is a ridged rod used for honing knives, a kitchen tool for putting an edge on blades.

clue.text: Girl holding tanpura's last to contribute Indian accompaniment

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the girl's name goes round the letter

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word tanpura

explanation.surface: A girl with a tanpura, an Indian lute, plays a final note as accompaniment to Indian music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompaniment' suggests music, but it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish served alongside curries, an accompaniment in Indian cooking.

clue.text: With some tremulousness, the setter's run into gritty case

indicators.note: into says the next pieces go inside the word for gritty

parts.note: a shingly case is a gritty, pebbly one, like a beach of shingle
the setter refers to themselves as I, so the setter's is I've, I have
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A nervous setter admits to rushing into a tough legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's is I'VE, as in 'the setter has'. 'Gritty' suggests determined, but here it means stony.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something shiveringly is to do it while trembling, so with some tremulousness.
